1 unchanged paragraph

• **Execution** is how each rule is kept. In [governs, enforces, attests](../../governs-enforces-attests.md) I described three levels: in the prompt, which is a hope; in hooks, which are deterministic but sit on the agent's own machine; or by a third-party system that does the blocking, which is the level we recommend. The test, from the ABP: "A control bounds a grant only if it is enforced by something the grant does not include." [Policy as code needs a policy first](../../policy-as-code-needs-a-policy-first.md) adds theonequestionmoremost frameworks miss:question: for every rule that is code, who can change that code.

1 unchanged paragraph

• **Agent identity** is the one we have written least about, and the speech is right to putputs it first. In the ABP it is implicit: a policy is for one agent in one deployment. The attestation layer in [governs, enforces, attests](../../governs-enforces-attests.md) makes it explicit: what was assured, at which policy version, signed so a third party can check it without taking the operator's word.
